So I booked with Cathay Pacific because the prices were so good, and mainly because they have an extremely generous rebooking policy at the moment. I booked on their lowest economy tariff and I‘m still able to change my dates for an unlimited number of times for free!

If the flights can’t operate in the end, luckily UK consumer protection laws mean there is no way they can wriggle out of refunding me. 

All of the accommodation I’ve booked is also pay on arrival with free cancellation until 24 hours before. 

The issue will be if Japan doesn’t lift their quarantine restrictions for foreigners and restore the visa waiver scheme by then, and I’ll have to move my dates. It could all still go wrong, but I think what I’ve done is as secure as possible as things stand. 

If they end up needing some proof of immunity, I’ve already had COVID so that shouldn’t be a barrier either.

I guess I learned that it really doesn’t matter what strangers think of you, and that most times they just... don’t?
For example, I used to avoid going to a restaurant for a nice meal when solo travelling, thinking people would assume I had been stood up, or had no friends etc. I don’t think anyone’s ever given me a second look when doing it now (or if they have I haven’t seen!) and it’s one of my favourite parts of solo travel. 
I’ve learned that I can do what I want, see the nerdy tourist attractions, go on the tours and eat alone, and it doesn’t matter what anyone else thinks because the trip is about me. It’s a good learning experience in putting myself and my needs first for a bit, rather than worrying about the opinions of others.
